nodes.title: Microsoft Entra ID: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) is the cloud identity provider behind Microsoft 365 and Azure. It authenticates users and apps and is the control point for access across the Microsoft cloud.

flashcards.front: What is Entra ID and how does it differ from on-prem AD?
flashcards.back: Entra ID is a cloud-based identity and access service using modern protocols (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML) over the internet. On-prem Active Directory uses Kerberos/LDAP inside a domain. They solve the same problem in different worlds and are often connected via hybrid identity.

flashcards.front: What are tenants, users, groups, and service principals?
flashcards.back: A tenant is one organisation's dedicated Entra directory. Users and groups are identities and collections for assigning access. A service principal is the identity an application uses to authenticate — the app equivalent of a user account.

flashcards.front: What is an Entra ID role vs an Azure RBAC role?
flashcards.back: Entra roles (e.g. Global Administrator, User Administrator) govern the directory itself — managing users, groups, and tenant settings. Azure RBAC roles govern access to Azure resources (subscriptions, VMs, storage). They are separate systems with separate assignments.

PIM provides just-in-time, time-bound, approval-gated elevation to privileged roles instead of standing admin access. Admins activate a role when needed; it expires automatically — reducing the attack surface of always-on privilege.

questions.q: Contoso owns the verified domain contoso.com in Microsoft 365. The administrator adds a second domain, contoso-eu.com, in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The new domain status remains Unverified after several hours. Which step is required to complete verification?
choices: Add the TXT or MX record provided by Microsoft to the public DNS zone for contoso-eu.com, then click Verify
Open a Microsoft 365 support ticket so the Domains team can mark the new domain as Verified
Synchronize the new domain to Microsoft Entra Connect from on-premises Active Directory
Assign the Domain Name Administrator role to the user attempting the verification
questions.explanation: Microsoft proves you control a custom domain by asking you to publish a TXT (or MX) record that it generates in your public DNS zone. Once the record is visible, the Verify action in the admin center succeeds and the domain becomes usable for Exchange Online, Teams, and Microsoft Entra ID. Support cannot bypass this check. Entra Connect synchronizes user objects, not domain ownership. The Domain Name Administrator role lets you manage domains but does not replace the DNS proof.

questions.q: You must give a help-desk analyst the ability to reset passwords for all non-administrative users and force them to change the password at next sign-in. The principle of least privilege applies. Which Microsoft Entra built-in role should you assign?
choices: Global Administrator — full control over every Microsoft 365 service
User Administrator — manage user accounts and most user properties
Password Administrator — reset passwords for non-administrators and other Password Administrators
Authentication Administrator — manage authentication methods for non-administrators
questions.explanation: The Password Administrator role is the narrowest built-in role that allows resetting passwords for non-administrative users and for other Password Administrators, which exactly matches a help-desk password-reset scope. Global Administrator grants far more than required and violates least privilege. User Administrator can change passwords but also create and delete users and manage groups. Authentication Administrator handles authentication methods (MFA, FIDO2, etc.), not routine password resets at the scale described.

questions.q: Contoso wants to ensure that every administrator must complete multifactor authentication when signing in, regardless of network location, while leaving standard users on their existing sign-in experience. Which Microsoft Entra feature should you configure?
choices: A Conditional Access policy that targets the directory roles you want to protect and requires MFA as the grant control
Security defaults at the tenant level, which apply MFA uniformly to every user account
Per-user MFA on the legacy MFA portal for each administrator individually
A sign-in risk policy in Microsoft Entra ID Protection that requires MFA only on high-risk sign-ins
questions.explanation: Conditional Access lets you scope a grant control such as Require multifactor authentication to a specific population — here the built-in directory roles for administrators — without affecting other users. Security defaults force MFA on everyone and cannot be scoped. Legacy per-user MFA works but is being deprecated, is harder to audit, and Microsoft now recommends Conditional Access for any granular policy. A sign-in risk policy only fires when Entra ID Protection rates the sign-in as risky, so an administrator on a known-good network would not be prompted.

questions.q: Your existing on-premises Active Directory forest has UPN suffix contoso.local. You plan to deploy Microsoft Entra Connect to synchronize identities to a tenant that uses contoso.com as its verified domain. What must you do before the first synchronization so users can sign in to Microsoft 365 with their on-premises credentials?
choices: Add contoso.com as an alternative UPN suffix in Active Directory Domains and Trusts, then update each user's UPN to use it
Rename the on-premises Active Directory domain from contoso.local to contoso.com using the rendom tool
Configure pass-through authentication first; Entra Connect will then accept the .local UPN as the sign-in name
Add contoso.local as a custom domain in Microsoft 365 so it can be verified and used as the sign-in suffix
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID will not accept a non-routable suffix such as .local as the sign-in name. The supported preparation is to add the verified public domain (contoso.com) as an alternative UPN suffix in Active Directory Domains and Trusts and then change each user's UPN to use it, so the synchronized UPN matches a verified domain in the tenant. Renaming the forest with rendom is disruptive and unnecessary. Pass-through authentication does not change UPN validation. You cannot verify a .local domain in Microsoft 365 because Microsoft cannot resolve a public DNS record for it.

nodes.title: Microsoft Purview: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft Purview is the data governance, compliance, and protection suite for Microsoft 365 and beyond — classification, data loss prevention, retention, eDiscovery, and insider risk. It's the compliance counterpart to the security stack.

flashcards.back: Sensitivity labels classify and protect content (e.g. Confidential) and can enforce encryption, watermarks, and access restrictions that travel with the file. Labels can be applied manually or automatically based on content (e.g. detecting credit-card numbers).

flashcards.front: What does Data Loss Prevention (DLP) do?
flashcards.back: DLP detects sensitive information (PII, financial data) across email, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and endpoints, and enforces actions — block, warn, or require justification — to stop it leaving the organisation. Policies are built from sensitive-info types.

flashcards.front: What is retention vs deletion in Purview?
flashcards.back: Retention policies and labels keep content for a required period (compliance) and/or delete it after a period (minimising risk). They resolve conflicts by a precedence order — retention generally wins over deletion to preserve records.

eDiscovery finds, holds, and exports content relevant to investigations or litigation across Microsoft 365. Legal holds preserve content in place so it can't be altered or deleted while a case is active.

questions.q: An administrator must protect Exchange Online users from messages that impersonate Contoso executives by spoofing display names and look-alike domains. Which Microsoft Defender for Office 365 policy should you configure?
choices: An Anti-phishing policy with user impersonation and domain impersonation protection enabled, listing the executives and the protected domains
An Anti-malware policy with the common attachments filter switched on for executable file types
A Safe Attachments policy in Dynamic Delivery mode targeting the executives' mailboxes
A Safe Links policy that rewrites every URL in inbound mail with the Microsoft scanning prefix
questions.explanation: Anti-phishing in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is the policy that specifically protects against impersonation: you list the user mailboxes (display names) and the domains (yours and trusted partners) to protect, and inbound mail that spoofs them is quarantined or flagged. Anti-malware blocks malicious attachments by hash or extension and does not handle display-name spoofing. Safe Attachments detonates attachments in a sandbox, and Safe Links rewrites and scans URLs at click time — both fight different attack vectors than impersonation.

questions.q: Contoso requires that confidential project documents stored in SharePoint Online and OneDrive be encrypted, watermarked with the user's email, and restricted so that only members of the Project Atlas group can open them, even after the file is downloaded or forwarded. Which Microsoft Purview feature should you use?
choices: Apply a sensitivity label that encrypts the content, adds a watermark, and grants Co-Author permission only to the Project Atlas group
Create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy that blocks the files from being downloaded outside the SharePoint site
Place the SharePoint site under a retention policy with a 7-year retain-and-delete action
Enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps file monitoring on the SharePoint site
questions.explanation: A Microsoft Purview sensitivity label can apply encryption, dynamic watermarks (including the recipient's email), and granular usage rights (such as Co-Author for one group) that travel with the file even after it leaves the tenant — exactly the protect-on-download requirement. DLP policies inspect content and block actions such as sharing or downloading but do not encrypt or watermark the file. Retention governs how long content is kept and does not control access. Defender for Cloud Apps gives visibility and session controls but does not embed encryption and permissions into the file itself.

questions.q: Microsoft Secure Score recommends that you reduce the attack surface by disabling legacy authentication protocols such as POP, IMAP, and SMTP AUTH for users that do not require them. Where in Microsoft 365 is the recommended way to enforce this for sign-ins?
choices: Create a Conditional Access policy that targets Other clients (legacy authentication clients) and uses Block access as the grant control
Disable basic authentication for each mailbox individually with Set-CASMailbox in Exchange Online PowerShell
Remove Office 365 licenses from any user who is detected using a legacy protocol so they cannot sign in
Configure an inbound mail flow rule in Exchange Online that rejects messages sent by Outlook 2010 clients
questions.explanation: The supported and recommended way to block legacy authentication tenant-wide is a Conditional Access policy that filters client apps to Other clients (legacy authentication clients such as POP/IMAP/SMTP AUTH and older Office apps) and applies the Block access grant control. Per-mailbox Set-CASMailbox toggles individual protocols but does not stop modern apps from using legacy auth, is harder to maintain, and is not how Secure Score measures the control. Removing licenses is punitive and does not prevent service principals or shared mailboxes from accepting legacy auth. Mail-flow rules act on messages after sign-in and do not stop authentication itself.

questions.q: A compliance officer must retain all Exchange Online mail and Teams chat for users involved in an active litigation matter, regardless of any user or retention-policy deletion, until released. Which Microsoft Purview capability should they use?
choices: Place the custodians on an eDiscovery (Premium) hold scoped to their Exchange and Teams locations
Apply a retention label that retains content for 7 years and then deletes it
Configure a Conditional Access policy that blocks the custodians from deleting their own messages
Enable Customer Lockbox for the tenant so Microsoft cannot service the custodians' data
questions.explanation: eDiscovery (Premium) — and the classic eDiscovery (Standard) — supports custodian-scoped holds that preserve mailbox content, including Teams chats stored in the user mailbox, in place even if the user or a retention policy attempts deletion. The hold can be released when the matter ends. A retention label or policy retains content but is broader and not tied to a custodian or matter. Conditional Access controls sign-in, not message deletion. Customer Lockbox governs Microsoft engineer access during support and does not preserve data.

nodes.title: Compliance frameworks: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Compliance is the discipline of mapping your controls to an external framework (PCI, HIPAA, SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001) and proving it to an auditor. Most exam questions test which framework owns which scope, not the minutiae of each clause.

flashcards.back: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard. Applies to anyone who stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data (PAN, expiry, CVV). 12 high-level requirements: firewalls, no defaults, encrypted storage, encrypted transmission, antivirus, secure dev, restrict access, MFA, log, test, policy. Required by Visa/Mastercard, not by law.

flashcards.front: HIPAA vs HITRUST — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: HIPAA is U.S. law for protected health information (PHI) — sets the legal requirements but is high-level on technical controls. HITRUST CSF is a certifiable framework that operationalizes HIPAA (plus ISO, NIST, PCI) into specific testable controls. Healthcare orgs are legally HIPAA-bound; many also pursue HITRUST cert to prove diligence.

American Institute of CPAs report on a SaaS company's controls across five trust criteria: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy. Type I = controls designed at a point in time. Type II = controls operated effectively over 6-12 months. Enterprise customers ask for the Type II as proof you're not making it up.

flashcards.front: GDPR — what does it require beyond US-style privacy laws?
flashcards.back: European General Data Protection Regulation. Requires explicit consent (not pre-ticked), right to access / deletion / portability, 72-hour breach notification, data protection officer (for large processors), data minimization, and Privacy Impact Assessments for high-risk processing. Fines: up to 4% of global revenue. Applies to anyone processing EU residents' data, regardless of company location.

questions.q: You want a single dashboard that correlates alerts from Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, Defender for Identity, and Defender for Cloud Apps into multi-stage incidents and supports automated investigation and response. Which portal should the security operations team use?
choices: Microsoft Defender portal at security.microsoft.com, which unifies Microsoft 365 Defender (XDR) signals and incidents
Microsoft Entra admin center, which surfaces sign-in risk events under Identity Protection
Microsoft Purview compliance portal, which centralizes labels, DLP, and eDiscovery
Microsoft 365 admin center, which exposes service health and message center notifications
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Defender portal (security.microsoft.com) is the unified Microsoft 365 Defender / XDR experience: it ingests alerts from Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, Identity, and Cloud Apps; merges related alerts into incidents; and runs automated investigation and response playbooks. Entra Identity Protection covers identity risk but not endpoint or email. The Purview portal handles information protection and eDiscovery, not XDR incidents. The Microsoft 365 admin center is for tenant administration and service health, not security analytics.

questions.q: Contoso wants new Windows 11 devices shipped from the OEM to be enrolled into Microsoft Intune and joined to Microsoft Entra ID automatically when the end user first powers them on and signs in with their work account. Which deployment method satisfies this requirement with no IT-staff touch on the device?
choices: Windows Autopilot user-driven deployment with the device hardware hash uploaded by the OEM and a deployment profile assigned in Intune
A Configuration Manager task sequence streamed over the internet via a Cloud Management Gateway
Group Policy auto-enrollment to Intune after the device is manually joined to the on-premises Active Directory domain
Provisioning packages (.ppkg) emailed to the end users so they can import the package after first boot
questions.explanation: Windows Autopilot user-driven mode is the zero-touch flow: the OEM uploads the hardware hash, you assign an Autopilot deployment profile in Intune, and the device runs through the out-of-box experience to enroll in Intune and join Microsoft Entra ID using the user's first sign-in. Configuration Manager requires existing infrastructure and a touch. GPO auto-enrollment depends on an on-premises domain join, which is the opposite of the cloud-only, zero-touch scenario. Provisioning packages still require manual import by the end user, so they are not zero-touch.

questions.q: An auditor asks for a record of every administrator action performed in Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Microsoft Entra ID for the past 90 days, exportable to CSV. Which Microsoft 365 feature should you use, and what is the prerequisite?
choices: Search the unified Audit log in the Microsoft Purview portal; the audit log must be turned on for the tenant (on by default for new tenants)
Run Get-AdminAuditLogConfig in Exchange Online PowerShell; this exposes the equivalent admin actions across all workloads
Open the Microsoft 365 admin center Reports blade; the Service usage reports cover administrator activity
Use Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps activity log; it must be connected to each workload with a separate API connector
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Purview unified Audit log records administrator and user activities across Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Teams, and Microsoft Entra ID, and supports filtering and CSV export. Auditing is now on by default for new tenants but the question's prerequisite is correct: it must be turned on (Start recording user and admin activity) before events are captured. Get-AdminAuditLogConfig only exposes Exchange admin auditing settings. The admin-center Reports blade shows usage analytics, not raw admin actions. Defender for Cloud Apps surfaces a subset of activities but requires connectors and is not the canonical audit-trail source.

questions.q: Contoso licenses some employees with Microsoft 365 E5 and others with E3. You must ensure that only the E5 users receive Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Power BI Pro from the E5 plan, and that you can swap E3 ↔ E5 assignments without removing users from the group that grants them other tenant services. Which approach should you use?
choices: Use group-based licensing on Microsoft Entra ID groups, disabling the specific service plans (Defender for Endpoint, Power BI Pro) on the E3 group's license assignment
Buy only E5 licenses and downgrade individual users by removing service plans manually in the admin center
Create separate tenants for E3 and E5 users and connect them with cross-tenant access settings
Assign each license directly to the user and write a PowerShell script that runs nightly to reconcile drift
questions.explanation: Group-based licensing in Microsoft Entra ID assigns a license SKU to a group and lets you disable specific service plans on a per-group basis, so an E3 group and an E5 group can grant overlapping baseline services while only the E5 group lights up Defender for Endpoint and Power BI Pro. Membership changes automatically reassign the correct plans, which is exactly the swap-without-removal requirement. Buying only E5 and downgrading by hand is costly and error-prone. Splitting into separate tenants destroys collaboration and breaks single-tenant requirements. Nightly PowerShell reconciliation is fragile and is the workaround group-based licensing was designed to retire.
